rows.label: A1
rows.predicate: The framed substrate: the symmetry-complete shell $\p=4\kap+1$ with its frame $(\chron;0,1,g)$ and derived quarter-turn, the orbital shell with its meridians and latitudes, and the stance under which the continuum is a projection.

rows.label: A2
rows.predicate: Finite-field algebra: the quadratic extension with its Frobenius conjugation and norm, Hilbert's Theorem~90, the square classes by Euler's criterion, the unitary group of a nondegenerate Hermitian form over a finite field.

rows.label: A3
rows.predicate: The continuum antecedents: the Cayley transform and the Crank--Nicolson step, Clifford algebras and the Dirac matrices, the $1{+}1$ Lorentz boost and its spin lift, the Schwinger unitary basis and the finite-field quantum mechanics it is compared with.

rows.label: A4
rows.predicate: The Hartley (max-)entropy reading of image counts, and reversibility as zero information loss.

rows.label: A5
rows.predicate: The laboratory Carrier $\Om=2\,408\,561$ with $\dS=602\,140$, and the constants correspondence read on the Carrier: the two-way constant has $c^2=2^{-1}$, a square since $\dS$ is even.

rows.label: A6
rows.predicate: The framework's stance: the primary object a finite symmetry space of algebraic possibilities, every description an incomplete projection; the theorems of the paper stand independently of it.

blocks.title: The shell, the coefficient field and the signature

rows.label: B1
rows.predicate: The shells in play and the two conjugation registers: the laboratory Subjects $\F_{13}$ and $\F_{173}$, the shell $\F_5$ for the dense computations, the coordinate shell $Y$ and the coefficient field $K$; $\im$ Frobenius-fixed, $\w$ anti-fixed; Carrier-scale statements are transfer targets, never sites of computation.

rows.label: B2
rows.predicate: The class is the datum: the nonsquares form one square class, and the Lorentzian form depends on its coefficient through that class alone.

rows.label: B3
rows.predicate: The drive is canonical: the drive multiplier is a nonsquare on every shell and the only named residue that is one on every symmetry-complete shell; the classes of $2$, $2^{-1}$, $-2$, $\pi=-2^{-1}$ and $\im$ are fixed by the parity of $\kap$, that of $e$ by no rule; the reframing flip keeps the class. Decided on $\p<2000$.
rows.source: Lem.~\ref{lem:canonical-nu}; rests on A2\newline \pywit{dirac}{p08009}{B3}, \leanwit{FrcCore}{p08009}{B3}, \leanwit{FrcMathlib}{p08009}{B3} \lean{Dirac.drive\_nonsquare, Dirac.named\_residues, Dirac.shell13, FRC.Dirac.drive\_nonsquare, FRC.Dirac.inv\_drive\_nonsquare, FRC.Dirac.quarter\_class, FRC.Dirac.two\_class}

rows.label: B4
rows.predicate: The factorisation of the temporal coefficient: $\nu=g=2^{-1}\cdot(2g)$ on every shell, the class of $2^{-1}$ even iff $\kap$ is even, the class of $2g$ odd iff $\kap$ is even, the product odd always; the reframing flip preserves the parity class and reverses the one-way direction.
rows.source: Cor.~\ref{cor:coefficient-factors}; rests on B5, B6\newline \pywit{dirac}{p08049}{B4}, \leanwit{FrcCore}{p08049}{B4}, \leanwit{FrcMathlib}{p08049}{B4} \lean{Dirac.nu\_factorisation, Dirac.two\_g\_class, Dirac.named\_residues, Dirac.shell13, Dirac.carrier\_constants, FRC.Dirac.nu\_factorisation, FRC.Dirac.carrier\_constants}

rows.label: B5
rows.predicate: The square class is chronon parity: the squares are the even drive steps, a residue's class the parity of its drive-step count; on $\kap$-even shells the whole quarter-turn group is square, so the order-four chart grading carries no signature. Decided on every primitive root of $\F_{13}$ and $\F_{173}$ and on $\p<2000$.

rows.label: B6
rows.predicate: Norm growth and parity: one chronon of drive scales every Frobenius norm by the square $g^2$; the single-chronon multiplier is odd and has no square root in $\Fp$; the flip $g\mapsto g^{-1}$ preserves the parity class.

rows.label: B7
rows.predicate: Signature lives on $\Fp$: the Euclidean form is hyperbolic and $Q_\nu$ elliptic, with the zero counts of the two classes on every symmetry-complete shell below $60$; over $K$ every element of $\Fp$ is a square and the dichotomy collapses.
rows.source: Rem.~\ref{rem:signature-record}; rests on D5\newline \pywit{dirac}{p08013}{B7}, \leanwit{FrcCore}{p08013}{B7}, \leanwit{FrcMathlib}{p08013}{B7} \lean{Dirac.ext\_square, FRC.Dirac.zeros5, FRC.Dirac.zeros13}

rows.label: B8
rows.predicate: One-way and two-way transport: comparison readings are even drive steps, the one-way single-chronon multiplier odd, and light-like transport carries no registered velocity, only its square class. Falsifier: a registered one-way velocity, or a two-way constant that changes under the synchronisation gauge.

rows.label: C1
rows.predicate: The Hermitian form on $K$-valued functions on a finite set: the sum of the conjugate of the first function times the second.

rows.label: C2
rows.predicate: The form is Hermitian and nondegenerate.

rows.label: C3
rows.predicate: The Cayley step of a Hamiltonian at a trace-zero parameter, and its recursion form.

rows.label: C4
rows.predicate: Exact Hermitian preservation: for a self-adjoint Hamiltonian and an admissible parameter the Cayley step is unitary.

rows.label: C5
rows.predicate: The finite Cayley transform: the scalar Cayley map is defined on the whole shell, takes values in the norm-one cycle, and bijects the projective line onto it, which has $\p+1$ elements and is the unitary group of one channel.
rows.source: Thm.~\ref{thm:cayley-transform}; rests on A2\newline \pywit{dirac}{p08019}{C5}, \leanwit{FrcCore}{p08019}{C5}, \leanwit{FrcMathlib}{p08019}{C5} \lean{Dirac.Ext.field, Dirac.Ext.cayley\_norm, Dirac.Ext.cayley\_injective, Dirac.Ext.card\_normOneGroup, FRC.Dirac.torus\_counts}

rows.label: C6
rows.predicate: The $\F_{13}$ Schr\"odinger example: the kinetic Hamiltonian is nilpotent, every trace-zero parameter is admissible, and every nonzero parameter gives a unitary step of order $13$.
rows.source: Ex.~\ref{ex:cayley-13}; rests on E7\newline \pywit{dirac}{p08020}{C6}, \leanwit{FrcCore}{p08020}{C6}, \leanwit{FrcMathlib}{p08020}{C6} \lean{Dirac.kinetic\_nilpotent, Dirac.cayley\_period, FRC.Dirac.cayley13\_values}

rows.label: C7
rows.predicate: The adjoint of a linear operator for the Hermitian form: the unique operator moved across the pairing; it exists because the form is nondegenerate and the space finite-dimensional.

rows.label: C8
rows.predicate: Translations are unitary: every translation operator preserves the Hermitian form, and its adjoint is the opposite translation.

rows.label: C9
rows.predicate: The finite Laplacian of an ordered basis is self-adjoint, each of its summands being self-adjoint.

rows.label: C10
rows.predicate: The finite Hamiltonian: the stiffness times the negative Laplacian plus a multiplication operator by a base-field potential; the stiffness $\vkap$ is distinct from the capacity $\kap$.

rows.label: C11
rows.predicate: Every finite Hamiltonian is self-adjoint: the Laplacian and the potential are, and the stiffness is Frobenius-fixed.

rows.label: C12
rows.predicate: The finite unitary group of a Hermitian space: the invertible operators preserving the form, the finite unitary group of the quadratic extension.

rows.label: C13
rows.predicate: Frame covariance: a change of basis by an invertible matrix intertwines, through the pullback of functions, the translations, the differences and the Laplacians of the two frames.

rows.label: C14
rows.predicate: The admissible set of a self-adjoint Hamiltonian: the trace-zero parameters at which the Cayley denominator is invertible; it contains zero.

rows.label: C15
rows.predicate: Finite periodicity: every Cayley orbit is periodic, the unitary group of the finite space being finite.

rows.label: C16
rows.predicate: The forward step: the orientation gauge $\alpha\mapsto-\alpha$ inverts every value of the Cayley map, the same $\Z_2$ as the derived orientation; the forward parameter composes the two quarter-turns and gives the finite Crank--Nicolson form at unit stiffness.

blocks.title: The Dirac operator and the boost transport

rows.label: D1
rows.predicate: Spinor fields on the coordinate shell, the forward differences, the gamma matrices for $\eta=\diag(-\nu,1,1,1)$, the standard finite Dirac operator and the finite Dirac equation.

rows.label: D2
rows.predicate: The Clifford relations of the gamma matrices.

rows.label: D3
rows.predicate: Dirac-to-Klein--Gordon factorization: the Dirac operator shifted by the mass, times its partner, is the spinorial Klein--Gordon operator shifted by the squared mass.

rows.label: D4
rows.predicate: The $1{+}1$ boost with its entries, the spin lift, the spinor transport and the transported Dirac operator.

rows.label: D5
rows.predicate: The boost group is the non-split cycle: the image of the extension's units with kernel the scalar line, the boost entries the coordinates of $z/\bar z$, cyclic of order $\p+1$; an order-three boost exists iff $3$ divides $\p+1$ (at $173$, not at $13$).
rows.source: Lem.~\ref{lem:boost-torus}; rests on A2, D14, D15\newline \pywit{dirac}{p08025}{D5}, \leanwit{FrcCore}{p08025}{D5}, \leanwit{FrcMathlib}{p08025}{D5} \lean{Dirac.Ext.boost\_eq\_one\_iff, Dirac.Ext.boost\_range, Dirac.Ext.exists\_boost\_eq, Dirac.Ext.card\_normOneGroup, Dirac.Ext.normOne\_cyclic, Dirac.Ext.order\_three\_iff, FRC.Dirac.torus\_counts, FRC.Dirac.triality\_values}

rows.label: D6
rows.predicate: Spin conjugation: the lift carries the two temporal gamma matrices to the stated combinations and fixes the other two.

rows.label: D7
rows.predicate: The pullback intertwines the differences of the two frames: the difference along a transported basis vector of the pulled-back field is the pulled-back difference.

rows.label: D8
rows.predicate: Exact covariance: the transport carries solutions of the Dirac equation to solutions of the transported equation; decided on a sample field at $\p=13$.

rows.label: D9
rows.predicate: The spinor form: under the plain conjugate transpose the gamma matrices carry mixed signs and the $\gamma^0$-twist fails; the odd product $X=\gamma^0\gamma^1\gamma^3$ is Hermitian with square $\nu$ and makes every gamma matrix anti-self-adjoint; the symmetric Dirac operator is self-adjoint and nilpotent for the $X$-form. Decided at $\p=5$, $13$, $173$.

rows.label: D10
rows.predicate: Exact Dirac evolution: the Cayley step of the symmetric Dirac operator shifted by the mass preserves the $X$-form; massless it is unipotent with order a power of $\p$; massive it is the norm-one phase of the mass times a unipotent, and its order is their least common multiple ($25$, $75$, $150$ at $\p=5$).
rows.source: Thm.~\ref{thm:dirac-evolution}; rests on C4, D9\newline \pywit{dirac}{p08030}{D10}, \leanwit{FrcMathlib}{p08030}{D10} \lean{Dirac.cayley\_unitary, Dirac.translation\_nilpotent}

rows.label: D11
rows.predicate: The two Dirac operators are one covariant family: the pullback identity holds for the symmetric differences, the transport carries the symmetric operator to its transported form, and the spinor form transports by the norm of the lift: norm-one lifts preserve it, the odd coset scales it by the nonsquare class.

rows.label: D12
rows.predicate: The worked shell $\F_{13}$ with the drive $2$: the boost at $x=y=1$ with $A=10$, $B=2$, the transported gamma matrices, the order $14$ of the boost cycle and no triality element; the named residues $2$, $2^{-1}$, $\im$, $e$, $\pi$ are nonsquares.
rows.source: Ex.~\ref{ex:dirac-13}; rests on D5\newline \pywit{dirac}{p08051}{D12}, \leanwit{FrcCore}{p08051}{D12}, \leanwit{FrcMathlib}{p08051}{D12} \lean{Dirac.shell13, FRC.Dirac.spin\_conjugation\_values, FRC.Dirac.torus\_counts, FRC.Dirac.shell173\_values, FRC.Dirac.triality\_values}

rows.label: D13
rows.predicate: Mass is winding rate: the finite Dirac equation equates the meridional development rate of the spinor field to the mass times the field, $E=hf$ an identity. Falsifier: a rest mass with no cycle winding, or a stationary state whose registered frequency is not its winding index.

rows.label: D14
rows.predicate: The boost is orthogonal: $\Lambda(x,y)$ preserves the coordinate form, by $A^2-\nu B^2=1$.

rows.label: D15
rows.predicate: The boosts form a subgroup of the orthogonal group: the product of two boosts is the boost of the product in the extension, the identity and the inverse are boosts.

rows.label: D16
rows.predicate: The explicit transported form: the transported Dirac operator is the Dirac operator of the transported frame with the transported gamma matrices, the spin conjugates of the standard ones.

rows.label: D17
rows.predicate: The transported gamma matrices satisfy the Clifford relations, conjugation preserving anticommutators.
rows.source: Cor.~\ref{cor:transported-clifford}; rests on D2, D16\newline \pywit{dirac}{p08070}{D17}, \leanwit{FrcMathlib}{p08070}{D17} \lean{Dirac.conj\_anticomm, Dirac.clifford}

rows.label: D18
rows.predicate: The transported factorization: the transported Dirac operator shifted by the mass, times its partner, is the spinorial Klein--Gordon operator of the transported frame shifted by the squared mass; decided as matrices and on sample fields.
rows.source: Thm.~\ref{thm:transported-factorization}; rests on D3, D16, D17\newline \pywit{dirac}{p08071}{D18}

rows.label: D19
rows.predicate: The worked shell $\F_{173}$, the second laboratory Subject, with the drive $2$ and $\im=93$: the boost at $x=y=1$ with $A=170$, $B=2$, the transported gamma matrices, the order $174$ of the boost cycle and its triality element; the named residues are nonsquares.
rows.source: Ex.~\ref{ex:dirac-173}; rests on B3\newline \pywit{dirac}{p08072}{D19}, \leanwit{FrcCore}{p08072}{D19}, \leanwit{FrcMathlib}{p08072}{D19} \lean{Dirac.shell173, FRC.Dirac.shell173\_values, FRC.Dirac.torus\_counts, FRC.Dirac.triality\_values}

rows.label: E1
rows.predicate: The image count and the loss factor of a finite map.

rows.label: E2
rows.predicate: A self-map of a finite set is bijective iff its image count is the whole count iff its loss factor is one.

rows.label: E3
rows.predicate: Cayley propagators have loss factor one: the Cayley step is invertible.

rows.label: E4
rows.predicate: Period dichotomy: kinetic Hamiltonians give unipotent propagators of order $\p$; potential Hamiltonians give diagonal propagators with phases on the norm-one cycle and order dividing $\p+1$ ($14$ at $13$, $174$ at $173$).
rows.source: Thm.~\ref{thm:period-dichotomy}; rests on C5\newline \pywit{dirac}{p08037}{E4}, \leanwit{FrcCore}{p08037}{E4}, \leanwit{FrcMathlib}{p08037}{E4} \lean{Dirac.cayley\_period, Dirac.kinetic\_nilpotent, Dirac.Ext.torus\_period, FRC.Dirac.cayley13\_values, FRC.Dirac.potential\_orders}

rows.label: E5
rows.predicate: The power map on the phase cycle has image count $(\p-1)/\gcd(\varepsilon,\p-1)$ and loss factor $\gcd(\varepsilon,\p-1)$, every nonempty fibre of that size.

rows.label: E6
rows.predicate: Boost transports have loss factor one: the pullback and the lift are bijective.

rows.label: E7
rows.predicate: Kinetic Hamiltonians are fully admissible: a nilpotent Hamiltonian, the kinetic Hamiltonian and the symmetric Dirac operator among them, has every trace-zero parameter admissible, on every shell.

rows.label: E8
rows.predicate: The three cycles in dynamical roles: the kinetic period is the register's, the potential period the third cycle's, the drive runs on the drive cycle; block compositions take the least common multiple, and the mixed instance at $\p=5$ has order $1563=(5^5+1)/2$; the general classification is posed as open.

blocks.title: The shell reading and the two spectra

rows.label: F1
rows.predicate: The four domains of one framed shell: the additive Fourier pair on the prime and the quarter-turn meridians, the multiplicative pair on the first latitude and the latitude one capacity step down; zonal and meridional motion; both dualities the index advance by the capacity.

rows.label: F2
rows.predicate: The latitude identities: the energy index $\kap+1$ is the first rung past the midpoint of the ladder; the shift by $\kap$ is multiplication by $g^{\kap}$ on the meridians and carries the first latitude to the energy latitude; $\kap=-4^{-1}$, so the energy radius is $3\cdot4^{-1}$ and $\pi=2\kap=-2^{-1}$; the unit-norm circle has $\p-1$ points. On $\F_{13}$ and $\F_{173}$.
rows.source: Prop.~\ref{prop:latitudes}; rests on A1\newline \pywit{dirac}{p08052}{F2}, \leanwit{FrcCore}{p08052}{F2}, \leanwit{FrcMathlib}{p08052}{F2} \lean{Dirac.latitude\_identities, FRC.Dirac.ladder, FRC.Dirac.four\_kappa, FRC.Dirac.terminal\_latitude, FRC.Dirac.torus\_counts}

rows.label: F3
rows.predicate: The free evolution is the drive: the drive pullback is unitary, the characters are its eigenvectors with the phase $g^{-k}$ per chronon, and every character line is isotropic except the two with eigenvalues $\pm1$, the meeting of the norm-one cycle and the drive cycle. Decided on $\F_{13}$ and $\F_{173}$.
rows.source: Thm.~\ref{thm:zonal}\newline \pywit{dirac}{p08040}{F3}, \leanwit{FrcCore}{p08040}{F3}, \leanwit{FrcMathlib}{p08040}{F3} \lean{Dirac.drive\_chi, Dirac.drive\_sum, Dirac.chi\_isotropy, Dirac.exceptional\_eigen, FRC.Dirac.drive\_eigen, FRC.Dirac.exceptional\_eigen, FRC.Dirac.isotropy}

rows.label: F4
rows.predicate: Two evolution sectors, one space: the drive's split-phase sector and the Cayley propagators' norm-one sector meet in $\{\pm1\}$ alone; the cycle Laplacian is self-adjoint, its Cayley steps commute with the drive, and the composite is unitary.
rows.source: Cor.~\ref{cor:sectors}; rests on C5, F3\newline \pywit{dirac}{p08041}{F4}, \leanwit{FrcCore}{p08041}{F4}, \leanwit{FrcMathlib}{p08041}{F4} \lean{Dirac.sector\_separation, Dirac.exceptional\_eigen, FRC.Dirac.sector\_separation}

rows.label: F5
rows.predicate: The shell reading: Schr\"odinger dynamics is the exact zonal evolution, Dirac dynamics the exact meridional development; the drive cycle holds the free evolution, the register the kinetic periods, the third cycle the interactions, masses and boosts; the light cone is a square-class boundary. Falsifier: a registered dynamics with a phase outside the cycles, or a mass without winding.
rows.source: Real.~\ref{rem:thesis}; rests on A4, B6, D5, D13, F3, F6

rows.label: F6
rows.predicate: The two spectra: the drive is semisimple with spectrum the drive cycle; the Dirac Cayley step at mass $m$ has the single eigenvalue $\varphi(-m)$ on the third cycle and the mass phases fill it once; the spectra meet in $\{\pm1\}$; the Hamiltonian form has the two eigenvalues $\varphi(\pm\im\nu m)$, a conjugate pair. Decided at $\p=5$, $13$.
rows.source: Prop.~\ref{prop:two-spectra}; rests on C5, D9, D10, F3, F4\newline \pywit{dirac}{p08048}{F6}, \leanwit{FrcCore}{p08048}{F6}, \leanwit{FrcMathlib}{p08048}{F6} \lean{Dirac.drive\_chi, Dirac.cayley\_nilpotent\_shift, Dirac.Ext.cayley\_injective, Dirac.Ext.card\_normOneGroup, Dirac.sector\_separation, FRC.Dirac.drive\_eigen, FRC.Dirac.sector\_separation, FRC.Dirac.torus\_counts}

rows.label: F7
rows.predicate: Finite plane waves, dispersion and the mass shell: the cycle Laplacian has the closed dispersion relation on the characters; the translations admit no characters and the kinetic sector is unipotent; the static massive Dirac equation has only the zero solution, the mass being an evolution phase.
rows.source: Prop.~\ref{prop:dispersion}; rests on C5, D3, D9, D10, E4, F3\newline \pywit{dirac}{p08077}{F7}, \leanwit{FrcMathlib}{p08077}{F7} \lean{Dirac.dispersion, Dirac.translation\_nilpotent, Dirac.cayley\_nilpotent\_shift}

rows.label: X1
rows.predicate: Two cycles for one unit circle: the continuum's single phase group appears on the shell as the drive cycle, carrying the free evolution, and the norm-one cycle, carrying the Cayley phases and the boosts, and the two meet in $\{\pm1\}$.
rows.source: Cor.~\ref{cor:explains}(i); rests on F4, F6\newline \pywit{dirac}{p08053}{X1}, \leanwit{FrcCore}{p08053}{X1}, \leanwit{FrcMathlib}{p08053}{X1} \lean{Dirac.sector\_separation, FRC.Dirac.sector\_separation}

rows.label: X2
rows.predicate: The one-way speed is gauge: the temporal coefficient is an odd drive step, registered transport is even, and the reframing flip reverses the one-way direction while preserving the parity class.
rows.source: Cor.~\ref{cor:explains}(ii); rests on B4, B5\newline \pywit{dirac}{p08054}{X2}, \leanwit{FrcCore}{p08054}{X2}, \leanwit{FrcMathlib}{p08054}{X2} \lean{Dirac.nu\_factorisation, Dirac.parity\_iff, FRC.Dirac.nu\_factorisation, FRC.Dirac.parity\_iff}

rows.label: X3
rows.predicate: Mass is an evolution phase, not a kernel condition: the symmetric Dirac operator is nilpotent, the static massive equation has only the zero solution, and the mass enters as the norm-one factor of the Cayley step.
rows.source: Cor.~\ref{cor:explains}(iii); rests on D10, F7\newline \pywit{dirac}{p08055}{X3}, \leanwit{FrcMathlib}{p08055}{X3} \lean{Dirac.translation\_nilpotent, Dirac.cayley\_nilpotent\_shift, Dirac.cayley\_unitary}

rows.label: X4
rows.predicate: The spinor form is forced: the continuum's $\gamma^0$-twist fails because Frobenius fixes the internal quarter-turn, and the arithmetic forces the twist onto the odd product omitting $\gamma^2$.
rows.source: Cor.~\ref{cor:explains}(iv); rests on D9\newline \pywit{dirac}{p08056}{X4}, \leanwit{FrcCore}{p08056}{X4}, \leanwit{FrcMathlib}{p08056}{X4} \lean{Dirac.spinor\_twist, Dirac.gamma\_dagger, FRC.Dirac.spinor\_form\_values}

rows.label: T1
rows.predicate: The classification of the admissible set of Cayley parameters for a general self-adjoint Hamiltonian, beyond the nilpotent and the diagonal cases.

legend.name: Import
legend.text: A standard result, a corpus result, or a convention used here without reproof, stated in Section~\ref{sec:primer} or at its site with its citation.

legend.name: Definition
legend.text: A naming, a declared dictionary, or a set-up move, carrying no empirical content.

legend.name: Theorem
legend.text: Proved at the statement the source column names, machine-verified in exact arithmetic by the named witness.

legend.name: Realisation
legend.text: States what a physical term denotes on the substrate: constitutive, not interpretive, and carrying its falsifier.

B3.name: FRC.Dirac.drive_nonsquare
B3.doc: 8:B3 — the drive is a nonsquare on every frame (`m = 1`).

B3.name: FRC.Dirac.inv_drive_nonsquare
B3.doc: 8:B3, 8:B6 — the reframing flip preserves the class: the inverse of the drive is a nonsquare (an odd power of `g`), so `[g⁻¹] = [g]`.

B3.name: FRC.Dirac.quarter_class
B3.doc: 8:B3 — `i` is a square exactly when the capacity is even (the eighth root of unity exists iff `8 ∣ p − 1`).

B3.name: FRC.Dirac.two_class
B3.doc: 8:B3 — `2`, `2⁻¹` and `−2` are squares exactly when the capacity is even (the second supplementary law at tier 0, 14-entropy's `two_is_square_iff`, and `−1 = (g^κ)²`).

B4.name: FRC.Dirac.nu_factorisation
B4.doc: 8:B4, 8:X2 — the factorisation of the temporal coefficient: `ν = g = 2⁻¹·(2g)` exactly on every shell (`h = 2⁻¹`), and the cofactor `2g` is a square exactly when `κ` is odd — the product `g` odd always (Corollary `coefficient-factors`); the one-way coefficient is the odd step `g`, the two-way constant the Carrier's.

B4.name: FRC.Dirac.carrier_constants
B4.doc: 8:B4 [value] — the laboratory Carrier `Ω = 2 408 561`: the two-way constant `c = 171 106` is a Carrier residue with `c² = 2⁻¹ = 1 204 281`, and the two factors compose, `2⁻¹ · (2g) = 1 204 281 · 12 = 6 = g`.

B5.name: FRC.Dirac.parity_iff
B5.doc: 8:B5, 8:X2 — the square class is chronon parity: on every frame, `g^m` is a square exactly when the drive-step count `m` is even (Theorem `parity`); registered transport `g²` is even, the one-way step `g` odd.

B6.name: FRC.Dirac.Ext.norm_scale
B6.doc: 8:B6 — norm growth: `N(c z) = c² N(z)` for every base residue `c`; one chronon of drive multiplies every norm by `g²`, a square.

B6.name: FRC.Dirac.Ext.mul_conj
B6.doc: 8:B6 — the norm is the product with the conjugate: `z z̄ = N(z)`, a base-field element.

B6.name: FRC.Dirac.inv_drive_nonsquare
B6.doc: 8:B3, 8:B6 — the reframing flip preserves the class: the inverse of the drive is a nonsquare (an odd power of `g`), so `[g⁻¹] = [g]`.

B7.name: FRC.Dirac.zeros5
B7.doc: 8:B7 [value] — on `𝔽₅` the Euclidean form has `5³ + 5² − 5 = 145` zeros and the Lorentzian form (`ν = g = 2`) has `5³ − 5² + 5 = 105`: the hyperbolic and the elliptic form part on the base shell.

C5.name: FRC.Dirac.torus_counts
C5.doc: 8:D5, 8:D12, 8:D19, 8:C5, 8:F2, 8:F6 [value] — the norm-one cycle: `|N¹| = 14 = p + 1` on `𝔽₁₃` and `174` on `𝔽₁₇₃` (both `ν = g = 2`); the unit-norm circle of the chart has `p − 1` points: `12` and `172` (8:F2).

C6.name: FRC.Dirac.cayley_period
C6.doc: 8:C6, 8:E4 — `DiracML.cayley_period`, its `let`-bound units opened: any proofs `hu`, `hu'` of the two units.

C6.name: FRC.Dirac.cayley13_values
C6.doc: 8:C6, 8:E4, 8:E7 [value] — the Cayley step of `H = −Δ` on `𝔽₁₃` has order exactly `13` at `α = w` and at `α = c = 6w` (`c² = 7 = 2⁻¹`).

D2.name: FRC.Dirac.clifford_values

D12.name: FRC.Dirac.shell173_values
D12.doc: 8:D12, 8:D19, 8:B3 [value] — the worked shells: on `𝔽₁₃` (`g = 2`, `κ = 3`) the quarter-turn is `i = 5`, `2⁻¹ = 7`, `e = g^i = 6` and `π = 2κ = 6`, and `2`, `7`, `5`, `6` are nonsquares; on `𝔽₁₇₃` (`g = 2`, `κ = 43`) `i = 93` with `i² = −1`, `2⁻¹ = 87`, `e = 2^{93} = 45`, `π = 86`, and `2`, `87`, `93`, `45`, `86` are nonsquares; the lift at `x = y = 1` has `δ = −1` on both, `A = (1 + ν)/δ = 10` and `170`, `B = −2/δ = 2`.

E4.name: FRC.Dirac.cayley_period
E4.doc: 8:C6, 8:E4 — `DiracML.cayley_period`, its `let`-bound units opened: any proofs `hu`, `hu'` of the two units.

E4.name: FRC.Dirac.cayley13_values
E4.doc: 8:C6, 8:E4, 8:E7 [value] — the Cayley step of `H = −Δ` on `𝔽₁₃` has order exactly `13` at `α = w` and at `α = c = 6w` (`c² = 7 = 2⁻¹`).

E4.name: FRC.Dirac.potential_orders
E4.doc: 8:E4 [value] — the potential propagator of `V = id` has order `14 = p + 1` on `𝔽₁₃` and `174` on `𝔽₁₇₃`, the least common multiple of the phase orders, every phase of norm one.

E5.name: FRC.Dirac.power_map13
E5.doc: 8:E5 [value] — on `𝔽₁₃`: the images of `x ↦ x^ε` have `(p − 1)/gcd(ε, 12)` elements — `12, 6, 4, 3, 2, 1` for `ε = 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12` (loss factors `1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12`).

F2.name: FRC.Dirac.ladder
F2.doc: 8:F2 — the ladder `1, …, 2κ`: `κ + 1`, the first rung past the midpoint `κ`, is still a rung.

F2.name: FRC.Dirac.four_kappa
F2.doc: 8:F2 — `4κ ≡ −1` on the shell (`4κ = p − 1`), so `κ = −4⁻¹` and the energy radius `1 + κ = 3·4⁻¹`.

F2.name: FRC.Dirac.terminal_latitude
F2.doc: 8:F2 — the terminal latitude: `π = 2κ = −2⁻¹`; the quarter-cycle shift `m ↦ m + κ` on the ladder is multiplication by `g^κ = −i` (`quarterTurn_eq_pow`, `i = −g^κ` by definition).

F2.name: FRC.Dirac.torus_counts
F2.doc: 8:D5, 8:D12, 8:D19, 8:C5, 8:F2, 8:F6 [value] — the norm-one cycle: `|N¹| = 14 = p + 1` on `𝔽₁₃` and `174` on `𝔽₁₇₃` (both `ν = g = 2`); the unit-norm circle of the chart has `p − 1` points: `12` and `172` (8:F2).

F3.name: FRC.Dirac.drive_eigen
F3.doc: 8:F3, 8:F6 — the drive pullback on the characters: with `y = g⁻¹`, `χ_k(g^{j}) = y^k · χ_k(g^{j+1})` for every `j, k` — the winding-`k` mode acquires the phase `g^{−k}` per chronon, so the drive is semisimple with the whole drive cycle as its spectrum (Theorem `zonal` (2), Proposition `two-spectra`).

F3.name: FRC.Dirac.exceptional_eigen
F3.doc: 8:F3 — the exceptional eigenvalue: `k = 2κ` gives `g^{−2κ} = −1` (and `k = 0` gives `1`) — the intersection `N¹ ∩ μ_{p−1} = {±1}` of the norm-one torus with the phase cycle.

F3.name: FRC.Dirac.isotropy
F3.doc: 8:F3 — isotropy: the character line `χ_k` is isotropic, `Σ_j χ_k(g^j)² = Σ_j g^{2jk} = 0`, unless `(p − 1) ∣ 2k`; on the two exceptional lines the sum is `p − 1 = −1 ≠ 0` (Theorem `zonal` (3)).

F4.name: FRC.Dirac.sector_separation
F4.doc: 8:F4, 8:F6, 8:X1 — sector separation: the inverse of the drive is primitive of order `p − 1` (`ord(g⁻¹) = p − 1`, so the free evolution is no Cayley step, whose scalar phases have order dividing `p + 1`), and the norm-one cycle meets the base field in `{±1}` alone (`u² = 1 ⇒ u = ±1`): the two spectra meet in the two signs.

F6.name: FRC.Dirac.drive_eigen
F6.doc: 8:F3, 8:F6 — the drive pullback on the characters: with `y = g⁻¹`, `χ_k(g^{j}) = y^k · χ_k(g^{j+1})` for every `j, k` — the winding-`k` mode acquires the phase `g^{−k}` per chronon, so the drive is semisimple with the whole drive cycle as its spectrum (Theorem `zonal` (2), Proposition `two-spectra`).

X2.name: FRC.Dirac.nu_factorisation
X2.doc: 8:B4, 8:X2 — the factorisation of the temporal coefficient: `ν = g = 2⁻¹·(2g)` exactly on every shell (`h = 2⁻¹`), and the cofactor `2g` is a square exactly when `κ` is odd — the product `g` odd always (Corollary `coefficient-factors`); the one-way coefficient is the odd step `g`, the two-way constant the Carrier's.

X2.name: FRC.Dirac.parity_iff
X2.doc: 8:B5, 8:X2 — the square class is chronon parity: on every frame, `g^m` is a square exactly when the drive-step count `m` is even (Theorem `parity`); registered transport `g²` is even, the one-way step `g` odd.
